# Enola CLI — Full Context for LLMs

> Enola CLI is a Rust command-line tool for self-hosting Tor hidden services (.onion), Git servers (Forgejo), CMS platforms (WordPress, Drupal, Ghost, Magnolia, Strapi, Wagtail), anonymous file sharing, WireGuard VPN, UFW firewall and AppArmor sandboxing on Debian/Linux — with post-quantum signed releases (ML-DSA-65, FIPS 204).

## What it is

- Product: `enola-cli`, a single Rust binary for end users. Current version: 0.2.0-alpha.
- Purpose: privacy-first self-hosting. Every service binds to 127.0.0.1 only and is exposed exclusively through Tor hidden services. Traffic model: `.onion:VIRTUAL_PORT → Nginx:INTERNAL_PORT → App:TARGET_PORT`.
- Platform: Debian/Linux (x86_64). Requires root (sudo), Docker, Nginx, Tor. `enola-cli setup` installs dependencies.
- License: source-visible proprietary. Free for personal, non-commercial use. No redistribution, no commercial use. Copyright (c) 2026 Salvador Palma Rodriguez.
- Security reporting: vulnerabilities must be reported privately to salvadorpalmarodriguez@gmail.com within 72 hours of discovery; public disclosure is prohibited until remediation (license §5).
- Architecture: hexagonal (ports & adapters). domain (pure logic) / ports (traits) / adapters (Docker, Nginx, Tor) / application (orchestration) / cli (routing) / infrastructure (utilities).

## Installation

```
curl -fsSL https://github.com/SalvadorPalmaRodriguez/enola-cli-lite/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sudo bash
```

The installer verifies SHA256 + minisign signature. Downloads can additionally be verified offline with the embedded post-quantum key: `enola-cli verify <file>`.

## Command reference (complete tree)

Global options: `--format text|json`, `--verbose`, `--binary-base-url <URL>`, `--web-url <URL>`, `--docs-url <URL>`, `--tor-socks <URL>`.

### tor — Tor hidden services
- `tor list` — list services with .onion addresses and ports
- `tor create -n <name> [-s web|static|files|raw] [-p <virtual-port>] [-t <target-port>] [--ssl]` — create a hidden service
- `tor start|stop <name>` — lifecycle
- `tor remove <name> [--force]` — delete
- `tor edit <name> [-p <port>] [-n <nginx-port>] [-t <target-port>] [--auto-ports]` — change ports
- `tor rotate <name>` — new .onion identity
- `tor auth list|enable|disable <service>` — client authorization
- `tor auth add <service> -c <client> -p <pubkey>` / `tor auth revoke <service> -c <client>`
- `tor auth generate -c <client>` — generate x25519 keypair (client side)
- `tor auth rotate <service> -c <client>` — rotate client keys (mitigates harvest-now-decrypt-later)

### git — Forgejo Git servers
- `git list` / `git create -n <name> [--ssl] [--http-port] [--ssh-port] [--admin-user <u> --admin-password <p>]`
- `git start|stop|status|delete <name>` — lifecycle
- `git registration <name> --enable|--disable|--status` — user self-registration
- `git edit <name> [--http-port] [--https-port] [--ssh-port] [--auto-ports]`
- `git publish <name> [--ssl]` / `git hide <name>` — Tor exposure
- `git user list|create|delete <server> [...]` — user management
- `git watcher` — pipeline watcher (foreground)

### CMS modules — wp, drupal, ghost, magnolia, strapi, wagtail
All share the same lifecycle: `list`, `create --name <n> --http-port <p>`, `start`, `stop`, `status`, `delete [--force]`, `publish` (expose on Tor), `hide`.
- `wp` — WordPress. Extra: `restart`, `update` (with backup), `config`, `edit [--http-port] [--https-port] [--ssl] [--auto-ports]`. Port range 8080-9000 (auto).
- `drupal` — drupal:10-apache + mariadb:10.11. Extra: `edit --http-port` (atomic container recreation).
- `ghost` — ghost:5-alpine + embedded SQLite, container port 2368. Extra: `edit --http-port`.
- `magnolia` — ghcr.io/magnolia-sre/magnolia-docker/magnolia-docker:latest (Tomcat, Java) with embedded H2 DB. Needs ≥4 GB RAM.
- `strapi` — Node + postgres:16-alpine. 6 per-instance secrets (db_password, app_keys, api_token_salt, admin_jwt_secret, jwt_secret, transfer_token_salt). Extra: `build-image [--force]` (build production image once before first create).
- `wagtail` — wagtail/bakerydemo:latest (demo site) + postgres:16-alpine, container port 8000.

### files — anonymous file sharing
- `files list` / `files create -n <name> [--auth] [--ssl]` / `files edit <name> [-p <port>]` / `files delete <name> --force` / `files fix-perms <name>`
- Files served from `/srv/enola-files/<name>/` via Nginx autoindex over .onion.

### maintenance
- `maintenance status|smoke-test|enable-checks|disable-checks|timer-status|ssh-config|backup`
- `maintenance ssh-harden-pqc [--dry-run] [--force]` — post-quantum SSH KEX (sntrup761x25519-sha512)
- `maintenance cleanup [--target all|logs|docker] [--dry-run] [--force] [--keep-days N]`

### diag — diagnostics
- `diag summary|nginx|tor|ssh|wordpress|wp-sync|nginx-test|resources`

### test / logs / ports
- `test run [-f filter]|list|benchmark|results|clean`
- `logs list` / `logs view <source> [-l N] [-f]` / `logs install` / `logs smoke-test`
- `ports list [--json]` — every port in the Tor→Nginx→App chain

### firewall — UFW
- `firewall setup [--ssh-port N] [--force]` — deny incoming, allow outgoing, allow SSH, DOCKER-USER chain
- `firewall status` / `firewall allow --port N [--proto tcp|udp|both] [--from CIDR]` / `firewall deny --port N [--proto]`

### apparmor — sandboxing
- `apparmor setup [--mode complain|enforce] [--force]` / `apparmor status`
- `apparmor mode --enforce|--complain|--disable [--profile <name>]`

### vpn — WireGuard
- `vpn create <name> [--port 51820] [--subnet 10.8.0.0/24] [--autostart] [--sync-firewall] [--tor]`
- `vpn list|start|stop|status|delete <name> [--force] [--sync-firewall]`
- `vpn peer add <iface> <peer> --endpoint <host> [--dns <ip>] [--psk] [--ip <ip>] [--tor]`
- `vpn peer add-pubkey <iface> <peer> <pubkey> <ip>` / `vpn peer remove <iface> <pubkey>`

### setup / doctor
- `setup` (core) / `setup --all` (core+VPN+security) / `setup --vpn` / `setup --security` / `setup --pqc-tls` (OpenSSL 3.5 + Nginx PQC stack)
- `doctor` / `doctor --security` (security audit: container hardening, configs, leaked secrets)

### update — advisory feed
- `update check [--json] [--force]` — exit codes: 0 OK, 11 critical advisory, 12 below min_supported, 20 invalid feed, 21 invalid signature
- `update schema [--json]` / `update verify-feed <source> [--signature] [--json]`
- `update download [--yes] [--dry-run] [--json] [--force] [--allow-unsigned]`
- `update apply [--binary <path>] [--json] [--allow-unsigned]`

### verify — post-quantum release verification
- `verify <file> [--pqsig <sig>] [--pubkey <key>] [--json]` — verifies ML-DSA-65 (FIPS 204) signature with the embedded public key; also verifies SHA256 if `<file>.sha256` exists. Offline.

### uninstall
- `uninstall` (dry-run) / `uninstall --yes [--keep-data] [--only binary,config,services,tor,nginx,systemd,apparmor,docker,ufw,data,deps] [--force] [--remove-deps]`

### docs — embedded offline documentation
- `docs quickstart|commands [group]|concepts [topic]|faq [term]|examples [case]|search <term>`
- `docs quantum-security|verify-downloads|security|install-from-iso`

### Other
- `license` — full license text
- `quickref` — Docker ↔ Enola equivalence table
- `web [--port 8090]` — local web dashboard, binds to 127.0.0.1, token-protected
- `config-show [--json]` / `config-validate [--reachable] [--json]` — centralized config (`~/.enola/config.toml`), priority: CLI flag > env var > file > default

## Key concepts

- Hidden service types: `web` (Tor→Nginx→App, recommended), `static` (Tor→Nginx, files from /var/www/<name>), `files` (Nginx autoindex), `raw` (Tor→App direct TCP, for SSH/databases).
- Everything is localhost-only: internal ports are never exposed to the network; visitors only ever see the .onion address.
- Tor client authorization uses x25519 keypairs (like SSH keys): client generates, sends public key to operator, operator authorizes.
- Post-quantum measures: ML-DSA-65 release signatures, optional ML-KEM hybrid TLS stack (`setup --pqc-tls`), WireGuard preshared keys (`--psk`), SSH sntrup761x25519 KEX (`ssh-harden-pqc`), Tor auth key rotation.
- Update security: advisory feed signed with minisign; binaries verified with SHA256 + minisign before applying; stable exit codes for scripting.
